column5: Description / How It Is Used in OSRS
Defines the real-world problem and desired outcome (e.g., standardizing floor plans for Power Apps). Ensures all design decisions align with operational and business value.

Defines the measurable operational outcome expected from the agent (e.g., reduce manual redesign effort, standardize layouts, improve onboarding speed). Prevents building AI systems without business value validation.
Defines who uses the output, what operational decision it supports, and what action will be taken. Aligns OSRS with Decision-First architecture principles.
Defines what the agent is (e.g., Deterministic Floor Plan Extraction Agent). Prevents the model from drifting into unrelated behaviors.
Defines the operational behavior style of the agent (e.g., deterministic, governance-first, literal interpretation, low creativity). Stabilizes behavior across models and workflows.
Defines what the agent must accomplish (Extract ? Normalize ? Structure ? Validate ? Output). Guides overall behavior.
Defines what the agent must not do (no hallucination, no reordering, no inference). Ensures deterministic and reliable output.
Defines execution flow (Extraction ? Validation ? Final Output). Prevents skipping steps and enforces human-in-loop process.
Breaks down the task into deterministic steps (area ? grid ? spaces ? groups ? normalization ? contract). Enables consistent reasoning.
Forces the agent to self-check before output (e.g., “Are all areas accounted for?”). Helps catch errors early.
Requires the agent to validate its own assumptions (e.g., group vs merged space). Prevents incorrect interpretations.
Encourages evaluating multiple interpretations (e.g., group vs repeated notes) before selecting the correct one. Improves accuracy.
Stops execution after extraction and requires user confirmation before producing final contract. Prevents propagation of errors.
Defines how uncertainty is handled (e.g., ambiguity, incomplete structure, conflicting interpretations). Prevents false confidence and unsafe assumptions.
Retains user-confirmed structure and corrections across steps. Prevents rework and repeated questioning.
Defines how external tools may be used (e.g., schema validation, renderer, Power Apps integration). Enables system expansion.
Defines how outputs are generated (human-readable Markdown + machine JSON). Templates guide AI behavior but do not enforce structure.
Ensures all outputs strictly conform to schema.json. This is the system-level guarantee for interoperability between agents.
Defines deterministic rendering rules (canvas size, typography, colors, spacing, alignment, Power Apps compatibility). Ensures consistent operational visual outputs across all rendered layouts.
Ensures extraction and reasoning decisions are explainable, reviewable, and traceable for governance and operational support.
Defines deterministic failure behavior and structured error responses when input validation, extraction, or contract generation fails. Prevents undefined system states.
Ensures safe handling of data (no unnecessary storage, compliance with standards like M365 when applicable).
Defines how the agent connects to external systems (e.g., Copilot, Power Apps, APIs). Keeps core logic decoupled from platform.
Defines framework version, agent type, owner, revision tracking, and operating specification references. Enables long-term maintainability and governance of OSRS agents.
